question: ctx_execute default timeout numeric value and its measurement spike are missing from TECH-SPEC Q8; v1 commit eea5877b (#406) explicitly removed a fixed default because it killed long builds — what is the actual ms value?

archaeology.INTRODUCED_BY: eea5877bd3925ec47018e3f305dd04cfc7868b0, Sun May 3 2026, 'fix(opencode-plugin+executor+routing): Mickey 3-issue + Issue #406 timeout policy'
archaeology.ORIGINAL_INTENT: Commit message: 'Zod .default(30000) ms timeout in ctx_execute / ctx_execute_file ... Server-side timeout policy is the wrong layer — every MCP host already enforces its own RPC timeout ... Drop the Zod .default(...) from all three tools timeout schemas; keep .optional(). When the caller omits timeout, no server-side timer fires (the host's RPC timeout governs). PolyglotExecutor: when timeout === undefined, do not set the setTimeout timer at all. Long-running processes complete naturally.'
archaeology.REGRESSION_RISK: v1 did not replace the removed 30000ms default with a different fixed number. It removed the server-side default entirely and left timeout undefined (no timer), relying on the MCP host's own RPC timeout. TECH-SPEC Q8 currently says 'one fixed default timeout, value set by measurement (not 120s, v1 #406)' which asserts a NEW fixed default exists and only its number is pending a measurement spike. That is not what v1 did: v1's fix was to stop having a server-side fixed default at all. If v2 ships any fixed default timeout (even a 'better' measured one), it reintroduces the exact bug #406 fixed — long builds get killed again once they exceed that number.
archaeology.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: Do not add a server-side default timeout to ctx_execute. Keep timeout optional with no default value; when omitted, do not start a setTimeout; let the host's RPC timeout be the only bound, exactly as eea5877b implemented it. If TECH-SPEC Q8 or ADR text require 'one fixed default timeout, value set by measurement,' that text contradicts the v1 fix and must be corrected, not implemented as written.

answer: There is no ms value to report because no such value exists in v1 or in any doc. Git history shows the opposite of what TECH-SPEC Q8 implies: commit eea5877b removed the one fixed default that existed (Zod .default(30000) ms) specifically because a 30s ceiling killed long builds (#406), and replaced it with no server-side default at all — timeout becomes optional/undefined, no setTimeout timer runs, and the MCP host's own RPC timeout is the only bound. TECH-SPEC Q8's line 437 ('one fixed default timeout, value set by measurement (not 120 s, v1 #406)') is a docGap: it asserts v2 will pick a new fixed-default number via a measurement spike, but no such spike is documented anywhere in TECH-SPEC, the ADRs, or review docs, and picking any fixed default (even a measured one) would re-break #406 the moment a build runs longer than that number. Recommendation for the owner: drop the 'fixed default, measured' language from Q8 and instead carry v1's actual fix forward — ctx_execute/ctx_execute_file timeout stays optional with no server default, no timer when omitted, host RPC timeout is the real bound. If a cap is still wanted for runaway processes, it must be a documented decision (new ADR), not retrofitted into Q8 as if a spike already set the number.

Drop the Zod .default(...) from all three tools' timeout schemas; keep .optional(). When the caller omits timeout, no server-side timer fires ... PolyglotExecutor: when timeout === undefined, do not set the setTimeout timer at all.' Compare docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md line 437: 'ctx_execute: one fixed default timeout, value set by measurement (not 120 s, v1 #406)' — this line's own parenthetical cites #406 but inverts its actual fix.
